newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH F.A. REJECT MIDDLESBROUGH POINTS APPEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH F.A. REJECT MIDDLESBROUGH POINTS APPEAL.

text.p: English premier league club Middlesbrough had their appeal against a three-point deduction rejected by the Football Association on Wednesday.
The premier league had imposed the penalty and fined the club 50,000 pounds ($80,000) after they called off their December 20 away fixture at Blackburn because of unavailability of players.

Middlesbrough, who claimed they would have had to field an under-strength side because 24 players were unavailable because of illness, injury and suspension, called off the game without permission from the league a day before they were due to play.

On Wednesday the three-man F.A. commission rejected the club's appeal against the deduction and fine and also awarded costs against the club. Blackburn's claim that they should be awarded the three points was also rejected.
The commission ruled Middlesbrough did not have just cause to postpone the match and, although it was accepted the club had acted in good faith, had committed a serious breach of league rules.

When the penalty was announced in on January 14 Middlesbrough were bottom of the league but a recent good run of results has moved them out of the relegation zone. On April 6 they will appear in their first major final when they play Leicester in the League Cup decider.
